title: Movie costumes show two sisters sharing clothes
summary:
A new movie of "Sense and Sensibility" is now in theaters. It is based on Jane Austen's first novel. It tells the story of two sisters. Elinor is sensible, and Marianne is romantic.

Costume designer Grace Snell made the clothes for the movie. The story takes place in England more than 200 years ago. Snell studied clothes from that time, but she also wanted them to feel modern.

Her big idea came from real life: sisters often borrow each other's clothes! After the family moves to a small cottage, the sisters share and mix their outfits.

At the fittings, Elinor's clothes were neat and organized. For Marianne, Snell brought boxes of ribbons and hats and let the actor dress herself. So Marianne has a playful style.

Snell gave both sisters jackets made from the same pattern and color, but in different fabrics. "They could wear the same outfit, but they were styled differently," Snell said.
why_it_matters: It shows that the clothes in movies are chosen on purpose to tell us about the characters, just like the clothes you pick can show who you are.
